read.thesis: Record Q2 with aggregates pricing up 5% on 2% volume and reaffirmed FY26 EBITDA of $8.1-8.5B, but ABS margins hit by haulage inflation and $8.5B Arcosa deal adds scale, not supply discipline.

capex.quote: Through the second quarter, we've invested approximately $800 million in growth CapEx

triggers.label: Aggregates pricing +5% on volume +2%
triggers.quote: Our aggregates volume increased by 2%, while pricing was 5% ahead.

triggers.label: FY26 EBITDA guidance reaffirmed $8.1-8.5B
triggers.quote: we are pleased to reaffirm our adjusted EBITDA guidance range for 2026

triggers.label: ABS haulage cost inflation hits margin
triggers.quote: we were impacted by cost inflation in the Americas Building Solutions business, and that is particularly in the area of haulage

triggers.label: New-build residential no recovery before late 2027
triggers.quote: at this stage, you got to say it's probably going to be in the back end of '27 at best before we see any recovery

guidance.quote: we expect full year adjusted EBITDA to be between $8.1 billion and $8.5 billion
net income between $3.9 billion and $4.1 billion
diluted earnings per share between $5.60 and $6.05
Capital Expenditure Guidance -- $2.7 billion to $2.9 billion

guidance.value: low single digit volume; broadly flat pricing
guidance.quote: outlook on cement kind of low single digit in terms of volume improvement and broadly flat on pricing
approximately $175 million of run-rate cost synergies to be achieved by year 3 with $60 million anticipated in the first year

red_flags.label: Net debt up to $15.4bn after M&A; buyback paused
red_flags.quote: Net Debt -- $15.4 billion at the end of the second quarter, reflecting an increase driven by acquisition and shareholder return spending.

red_flags.label: ABS margin decline on haulage inflation
red_flags.quote: we were impacted by cost inflation in the Americas Building Solutions business, and that is particularly in the area of haulage

evasions.quote: What do you think it would take to get cement pricing moving up stronger than what we're seeing today
